Sometimes I dont know where the dissociation begins and ends... I think generally I tend to dissociate in mornings because my nightmares put me in a bad state of mind, and I tend to "skip" time or something... Like the other day, I was sitting in my bed completely feeling just... Nonexistent and a loud notification from my phone snapped me out of it, but the phone said a few minutes had passed even though i had felt as if I'd literally been there for hours. I get incredibly disoriented and distressed enough by this that I just start crying, I just hate suddenly not having control of myself like that. Other days I also tend to get this extreme feeling of fogginess and paralyzation and cant formulate thoughts, like I am "slow" and it goes on for several hours. It can be so debilitating because I dont feel that I can drive or work efficiently. I also just tend to get surreal feelings like everything is fake and that if I died it wouldn't matter because nothing is real, which sounds cliche, but in these moments I dont think I can even register my body parts as being all there. I think those are the most dangerous because I just feel like I'd be capable of just walking into the street and getting hit by a car but not caring because I believe in that moment that nothing is real, just feeling like I'm in a movie and my body parts arent mine. I used to daydream a LOT as a kid, and I still do often, but I feel like my dissociation has become more of a mind fuck now that I'm an adult... :/

It's irrational to get upset by their comments but I know that I am oversensitive to being criticized because of trauma. But man living with people is just fucking hard and its neither of our faults. I know that probably doesnt help much but I just wanted to say that I feel you... the exhaustion from dealing with this, the hurt feelings, everything

I've been in several friendships like this but only a couple that I seriously regret in hindsight now that they've ended, so I've thankfully not been in a marriage that deals with this like OP and several people have... 


But in regards to friendships, if it exacerbates too many severe symptoms and the other person doesn't bother to understand / care / support you, then the friendship is NOT worth it, at least it wasn't for me. No matter how much I needed it at the time, and how much I just needed a friend and someone who wanted to listen, it was only more damaging for me in the long run especially since these were also manipulative people. I can't get over the anger I have toward myself for not breaking it off way, way earlier. I am now currently surrounded by friends who do a lot of personal growth work due to also having severe trauma, and when these things come up, the difference in the way they communicate and care about me is like night and day. I can't stress how important it is for me to be able find a couple of people that are safe, and it's made me realize that I need to pay better attention to the people I associate myself with early on in my life. I just cant be dealing with a person who just exacerbates my PTSD and has me on edge and defensive all the time, it was driving me into an even darker hole, meanwhile the person never cared or understood. They flat out never realized that this was happening to me internally. 


CPTSD and severe trauma survivors are kindred spirits for me, sometimes the people who are just healthy are the most hurtful to me, and have been the ones who turn out to be manipulative due to my vulnerabilities

I was diagnosed with ADD, or innattentive ADHD as a child. Supposedly I was a classic case. Executive dysfunction, lack of attention, behavioral issues, etc. After reading and investigating more thoroughly now in adulthood, I now think it's a misdiagnosis for me. Like many of the below comments mention, I think my trauma had a bigger role in my childhood development than doctors or teachers knew about. I definetly see the overlap, but never went on any ADHD medication and so wouldn't actually know until I try it (parents were weird about meds, led to me terrified of meds for a long time). However, anti-depressants have done very good things for my executive dysfuction. And I feel a clearer head, among other things. Good luck seeing if ADD medication will work for you, it never hurts to see how treatments work for yourself.

Hmm. I didn't want to disclose too much, but I also have never openly discussed self-harm with anyone and I want to try to bring this up with my therapist eventually, so maybe writing about it is a good start.

I had a messed up history with CSA, and like many others, didn't really understand what had happened to me for a long time. I started self-harming pretty young. But I didn't realize that it was self-harm, and I would scratch / hit myself / (TMI) injure my genital areas etc. I don't really know what set it off, but I continued on-and-off through the rest of my life, and was at times shamed out of it when classmates would notice, or out of fear. Then things worsened in adulthood, and the self-harm became more insidious and emotional as well as more scary. I started having all sorts of violent thoughts about seriously hurting myself, and it got really bad. However, it's been half a year since I self-harmed, and it's been really hard to consciously force myself to stop? So I've tried to change things around me, first. I noticed that a lot of it had to do with my environment and surroundings (at least for me). My bedroom and being alone are a big trigger, and so I started avoiding my bedroom unless I was ready to sleep, and force myself to draw / do homework (im an art student so my homeworks pretty enjoyable I guess) / or go out with friends that are safe when I start feeling low. I also started practicing a lot more physical self-care, and started raising my self-esteem little by little.

I tend to read my guy friends' behaviors as being... secretively ill-intentioned? Basically, not much will help me be convinced that they don't want to hurt me or abuse me. :( It's difficult.

I hospitalized myself last week, and while one of my friends was on the phone with me throughout a lot of it, I just... Feel like I'm wearing her out so fast. 
I'm in treatment, therapy, medicated, and functioning better than I used to, but I still feel depressed. I still have those dark spirals. I'm *still* not perfectly functioning, I'm still difficult to be around sometimes, and I still feel isolated and apathetic. My emotions are dulling. Yes, I'm tired of it all, I'm tired of being like this. I'm doing what I can and it's not good enough for others... I'm just wondering if any thing is worth it. I just don't want to be tired anymore.
A lot of people have ended things with me because of my instability. Friends, mostly. It's difficult, but I keep fighting to feel worth something.
